## Investigation summary

**Bottom line:** The user-visible degradation is slow admin user listing. The primary root cause is a fixed ~1.65 s latency inside `ts-admin-user-service`, in the `AdminUserController.getAllUsers` handler behind `GET /api/v1/adminuserservice/users`. I found one additional anomaly (HTTP 403s on `POST /api/v1/adminuserservice/users`) that is lower confidence and may be a separate fault.

### Affected endpoints

| Endpoint (service) | Abnormal avg | Normal avg | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/v1/adminuserservice/users` (ts-ui-dashboard) | ~1657 ms | ~10 ms | 49 requests, all 200 |
| `GET /api/v1/adminuserservice/users` (ts-admin-user-service) | ~1653 ms | ~9.4 ms | 53 requests, all 200 |
| `POST /api/v1/adminuserservice/users` | ~36 ms | ~81 ms | Latency is not regressed; see 403 note below |

Every other Server span I compared stayed within normal ranges. The login path (`ts-auth-service` `getToken`, ~74 ms) matches its baseline. Verification-code, route, and travel2 log errors are present in baseline with the same character.

### Root cause 1: fixed latency in ts-admin-user-service `getAllUsers`

- **Where the time goes:** The downstream call to `ts-user-service` (`GET /api/v1/userservice/users`) completes in ~6–10 ms. The remaining ~1640 ms is self-time inside `ts-admin-user-service`, in `AdminUserController.getAllUsers`.
- **Shape of the delay:** All 53 GET requests fall in a tight 1649–1657 ms band. That is a constant injected delay, not load-dependent queueing. The same ~1650 ms appears in every minute of the abnormal window.
- **Resources are not the cause:** CPU usage is about 0.011 cores, lower than baseline. Memory is at baseline (~15% of limit), there are no major page faults, no network errors, and no restarts.
- **Logs:** The `[getAllUsers]` log lines show normal "success" messages with no errors or warnings, consistent with a delay inside the handler rather than a failure.

**Propagation:** `loadgenerator` → `ts-ui-dashboard` (`GET /adminuserservice/users`, ~1661 ms) → `ts-admin-user-service` (`getAllUsers`, ~1653 ms self-time) → `ts-user-service` (fast, ~8 ms). The fault originates in `ts-admin-user-service`; `ts-ui-dashboard` only passes the latency through.

### Secondary anomaly (lower confidence): 403s on admin-user create

- `POST /api/v1/adminuserservice/users` returned HTTP 403 in 31 of 53 abnormal traces, versus 3 of 32 in normal traces. `ts-ui-dashboard` shows 30 of 49 such responses.
- The 403 is generated by `ts-admin-user-service` itself (`sendError` at ~2 ms, no downstream call), so it is an in-service authorization or validation rejection, not propagation.
- There are no matching ERROR/WARN log lines for these requests, and the pattern is spread evenly across the window.
- It could be a separate authz fault or a test-traffic artifact. The data does not settle which. It needs a check of the auth/permission path for this endpoint before it is ruled in or out as a second root cause.

### Ruled out

- **ts-auth-service login path:** matches baseline.
- **ts-route-service "Route not found" errors:** present in baseline, not a regression.
- **Resource saturation in any service:** not indicated in the admin-user-service metrics I checked.
